_meta.purpose: Single source of truth for ADHD terminology. Dual-use: (1) teach learning-reference, (2) MDX <Term> component source in the blog (dashed underline + hover/click definition).

evidenceLegend.verified: Passed adversarial verification against a primary/peer-reviewed source.
evidenceLegend.gathered: From a fetched source with a pulled quote; not machine-verified. Re-check before publishing.
evidenceLegend.practitioner-framework: Widely-used practitioner concept, NOT peer-reviewed. Frame as such — never cite as science.
evidenceLegend.needs-source: Stub. Do not write a definition until a trusted source is attached.

_meta.schemaNote: shortDef = tooltip text (one sentence). longDef = expanded/click. agentAngle = the bridge to coding-agent workflow (series-specific).

terms.shortDef: The brain's management system — planning, prioritizing, initiating, and switching between tasks.
terms.longDef: The set of top-down cognitive control processes used to plan, prioritize, start, sustain, and switch tasks. ADHD is characterized by executive dysfunction: the gap between forming a plan and executing it. Task completion is hard without externally imposed structure (e.g. deadlines).

sources.label: arXiv 2507.06864 (names EF mechanisms for knowledge work)

terms.agentAngle: A coding agent holds and executes the chain a plan needs to survive — it fills the plan→action gap where the plan would otherwise 'evaporate'. The agent acts as externalized executive function.

terms.shortDef: The small mental scratchpad that holds information 'live' while you use it — measurably reduced in ADHD.
terms.longDef: The limited-capacity system for temporarily holding and manipulating information. A meta-analysis of 38 studies found moderate-magnitude working-memory deficits in adults with ADHD versus controls, across both phonological and visuospatial domains, and these persist into adulthood.

sources.label: Alderson et al. — WM deficits in adult ADHD (meta-analysis, 38 studies)

terms.agentAngle: The core bridge of the series: because holding state in working memory costs energy an ADHD brain can't spare, offloading it — named sessions, memory files, written plans — is externalizing working memory, not just 'being organized'.

terms.shortDef: The hidden tax of resuming interrupted work — and it's paid in stress, not just time.
terms.longDef: Field research on information workers found tasks switch roughly every ~11 minutes, and returning to an interrupted task can involve attending to ~2 other topics first. Critically: interrupted work was completed FASTER, not slower — but at significantly higher stress, frustration, and mental workload (p<.01), with as little as 20 minutes enough to spike it. (The popular '23 min 15 sec to refocus' figure has no traceable primary source — do not cite it.)

sources.label: Mark et al. 2005 — No Task Left Behind (CHI'05)
Mark et al. 2008 — The Cost of Interrupted Work (CHI'08)

terms.agentAngle: Running N parallel agents manufactures constant self-interruption. The trap: it can make you finish faster while quietly torching your stress budget — the double-edged sword in one mechanism.

terms.shortDef: Working alongside another present-but-passive person to anchor focus and accountability.
terms.longDef: Doing a task in the presence of someone 'simply there, working on their own thing, not helping or supervising.' Functions as external executive functioning. A small VR study (n=12) found an AI body double improved focus/task performance comparably to a human one (no significant efficiency difference, p=1.000). Note: direct trial evidence overall is minimal — plausible/cheap/safe rather than proven.

sources.label: arXiv 2509.12153 — Body doubling for ADHD in VR

terms.agentAngle: Pairing with an agent ≈ a digital body double: a co-present collaborator that keeps you engaged and accountable, delivering the body-doubling benefit without another human in the room.

terms.shortDef: An intense, time-distorting absorption in a task — ADHD's double-edged gift.
terms.longDef: A state of intense, time-distorting concentration that enables deep work but causes loss of track of other obligations (meetings, meals, schedules). Often framed as a perk, but the time-blindness that comes with it is the cost.
terms.agentAngle: The agentic-coding era is unusually hyperfocus-friendly — but agents also make it easy to fall down ten parallel rabbit holes at once, amplifying both the gift and the chaos.

terms.shortDef: Difficulty perceiving and estimating the passage of time.
terms.longDef: STUB — a time-perception meta-analysis (27 studies) exists but skews child/adolescent; needs an adult-focused source before a confident definition ships.

sources.label: Time perception in ADHD (meta-analysis, 27 studies) — verify adult applicability

terms.agentAngle: TBD — likely relates to losing hours in an agent session; confirm with source first.

terms.shortDef: Practitioner framework (Dodson): ADHD attention is driven by interest/novelty/urgency, not importance.
terms.longDef: STUB — a popular framing from Dr. William Dodson that ADHD motivation is gated by interest, novelty, challenge, and urgency rather than priority. NOT peer-reviewed. If used, frame explicitly as a practitioner model, never as established science.
terms.agentAngle: TBD — explains the dopamine pull of a fast agent feedback loop; find a citable primary before leaning on it.

terms.shortDef: The total mental effort a task demands of working memory at once.
terms.longDef: STUB — needs a trusted cognitive-load-theory source (Sweller) attached before shipping a definition; currently only referenced indirectly via the interruption/working-memory sources.
